process_completion_semantics.scope: Every prerequisite command, deployment command, verification GET command, metadata command, and the 300-second observation process/window.
process_completion_semantics.single_invocation_rule: Starting a command creates one invocation. If that invocation yields a running cell, session, or process ID instead of an immediate terminal result, it remains the same single invocation.
process_completion_semantics.continuation_rule: Use only the environment's wait, poll, or resume mechanism on that exact yielded ID until that same process returns exactly one terminal exit status and complete output. Waiting, polling, or resuming the same exact ID is not a retry, substitution, or second invocation.
process_completion_semantics.never_restart_rule: Never start the command again after an ID has been yielded. A replacement invocation, alternate command, or new process is forbidden.
process_completion_semantics.terminal_ambiguity_rule: Loss of the exact running ID, process termination without a final exit status, inability to continue waiting or polling that same ID, multiple terminal statuses, or incomplete terminal output is terminal ambiguity. Stop and preserve evidence; do not retry or substitute.
process_completion_semantics.accounting_rule: Record invocation_count separately from wait_poll_count for every command. Where the packet says once, require invocation_count exactly 1; wait_poll_count may be zero or greater and does not change invocation_count.
process_completion_semantics.observation_rule: The 300-second observation is one observation invocation and one continuous version-bound window. A normal tool yield requires same-ID waiting or polling until the single terminal result and complete window output; it must not manufacture ambiguity or restart the window.
